sentences.text:
Manoj Kumar Gupta And Another vs State Of Up And 3 Others
on 9 July, 2024

Author: Rajiv Gupta
Bench: Rajiv Gupta
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:110890-Db
Court No. - 47
Case :- Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. - 11449 of 2024
Petitioner :- Manoj Kumar Gupta And Another
Respondent :- State Of Up And 3 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Ajay Kumar Kashyap,Vishakha Dubey

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Rajiv Gupta,J.
Hon'ble Surendra Singh-I,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned Aga for the State and perused the record.

2.  Although, the prayer made in this writ petition is to quash the FIR dated 26.05.2024 arising out of Case Crime No.282 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 406, 323, 504, 354 IPC and Sections 3/4 D.P.
Act, Police Station Sikandara, District Agra, but when the matter has been taken up, learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that all the offences, complained of, are punishable up to seven years and therefore, before effecting the arrest of the petitioners, specific provisions contained in Manoj Kumar Gupta And Another vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106538468/
1 Section 41(1)(b) and Section 41-A of CrPC be strictly complied with in view of law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in several judgments.

entities.text: Manoj Kumar Gupta And Another vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. We have perused the FIR, which prima facie discloses the cognizable offence against the petitioners and therefore, the prayer made to quash the FIR cannot be entertained in view of law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State of Telangana Vs. Habib Abdullah Jellani reported in (2017) 2 SCC 779 and Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. Vs. State of Maharashtra and Others

entities.text: State of Telangana Vs. Habib Abdullah Jellani reported in (2017) 2 SCC 779
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. Vs. State of Maharashtra and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
and as such, we are of the view that no interference is warranted.
4.

However, considering the fact that all the offences, complained of in the impugned FIR, are punishable with a term up to 7 years, therefore, in case of effecting the arrest of the petitioners in pursuance of the impugned FIR, it is directed that the respondents/ authorities shall ensure that the specific provisions contained in Section 41(1)(b) and Section 41-A of CrPC and the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar reported in (2014) 8 SCC 273 as well as the directions issued in judgement and order dated 28.01.2021 of this Court passed in Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 17732 of 2020 (Vimal Kumar and 3 Others Vs. State of U.P. and 3 Others) reported in 2021 (2) ACR 1147, be strictly complied with.
5. With the aforesaid observations, the instant writ petition stands disposed of.
Order Date :- 9.7.2024 Subham  Manoj Kumar Gupta And Another vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106538468/
